citations.title: Application of Lean Six Sigma in healthcare: a systematic review
citations.what_it_says: Systematic review documenting widespread adoption of LSS in hospital operations and quality roles, with certified Green/Black Belt practitioners commonly leading DMAIC projects.

citations.authors: Niemeijer GC, Trip A, Ahaus KTB, Does RJMM, Wendt KW
citations.title: The effectiveness of Lean Six Sigma in healthcare: a systematic review
citations.journal: International Journal for Quality in Health Care
citations.what_it_says: Finds that LSS-trained leaders deliver measurable process improvements in clinical operations, supporting demand for certified belts in ops leadership roles.

citations.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical and Health Services Managers
citations.what_it_says: Reports 2024 median wage of $110,680 and 28% projected growth (2023-33) for health services managers, the role cluster most frequently filled by LSS-credentialed clinicians moving into ops.

citations.authors: Antony J, Sunder M V, Sreedharan R, et al.
citations.title: Lean Six Sigma in healthcare: a taxonomy of critical success factors
citations.what_it_says: Identifies certified Belt-led teams as a critical success factor for healthcare process improvement, reinforcing employer demand for credentialed staff.

citations.title: ASQ Global State of Quality and Salary Survey
citations.what_it_says: Reports Black Belts earn approximately 10-20% more than non-certified peers in healthcare and that certification is a common gating credential for quality manager roles.

citations.authors: DelliFraine JL, Langabeer JR, Nembhard IM
citations.title: Lean Six Sigma for the healthcare practice: a pocket guide and case for clinician leaders
citations.what_it_says: Argues LSS provides clinicians a structured path into operational leadership, framing the credential as a bridge from bedside to administrative and improvement roles.
